turns.user: For a 3DCP mortar with w/b 0.35, s/b 1.5, 90 % OPC + 10 % silica fume and 0.6 % PCE, plot the Bingham flow curve up to 100 1/s and the structuration curve over 45 minutes of rest, and compare both with measured literature curves.
turns.text:
I’ll check the mix conventions, predict both curves, and retrieve comparable measured literature curves. I’ll state any defaults and distinguish model estimates from measurements.
Both plots are generated with measured analogue curves overlaid. The structuration-rate model is weak and its uncertainty band is broad, so the literature curves are the primary evidence. The database query rejected a separator inside the query text; I’ll retry with a simpler query to check the analogue values and sources.
Created both plots with literature analogue overlays and shaded q10–q90 prediction bands:

- [Bingham flow curve PNG](</C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261017-015322-8042/flow_curve_OPC90_SF10_PCE06_3DCP.png>) · [CSV](</C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261017-015322-8042/flow_curve_OPC90_SF10_PCE06_3DCP.csv>)
- [Structuration curve PNG](</C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261017-015322-8042/structuration_OPC90_SF10_PCE06_3DCP.png>) · [CSV](</C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261017-015322-8042/structuration_OPC90_SF10_PCE06_3DCP.csv>)

| Predicted quantity | q50 [q10, q90] |
|---|---:|
| Dynamic yield stress | 234 [16, 843] Pa |
| Plastic viscosity | 6.43 [0.84, 33.13] Pa·s |
| Shear stress at 100 s⁻¹ | 1,023 [250, 3,901] Pa |
| Initial static yield stress | 271 [22, 9,125] Pa |
| Structuration rate, Athix | 0.697 [0.023, 13.669] Pa/s |
| Static yield stress after 45 min | 4,003 [307, 61,123] Pa |

The curves use \(\tau=\tau_0+\mu\dot\gamma\) and \(\tau_s(t)=\tau_s(0)+A_{\mathrm{thix}}t\). Their plotted medians come from sampled parameter distributions; they need not equal curves calculated from the separate parameter medians.

The literature comparison shows:

- **Flow:** [Fig. 20, DOI 104158](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2021.104158) gives experimental Bingham fits reaching **202.2 Pa** for SF-6% and **309.17 Pa** for SF-10% at **100 s⁻¹**. Both are below the predicted median. These analogues share **w/b 0.35**, but use **s/b 1**, so they are not composition matches. The overlaid points reconstruct published fit equations rather than raw measurements. The additional [NZ-0 analogue](https://doi.org/10.3390/buildings16030490) contains digitized loading/unloading branches measured at different material ages.
- **Structuration:** [Fig. 8, DOI 105509](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2024.105509) provides digitized R20/R40/R60 curves. At **40 min**, their measured static yield stresses are **2,850, 1,780 and 620 Pa**, respectively. They vary nonlinearly, whereas the prediction assumes linear buildup. Their clock measures time after water addition, so comparison with uninterrupted rest is approximate.

**Athix is a weak model: treat the structuration prediction as order-of-magnitude guidance and the published curves as primary evidence.** The wide bands preclude precise rheological specification; experimental verification is needed.

Defaults used: natural sand; PCE dosage interpreted as product mass relative to binder. The tool also populated age **28 d**, **comp_cube50**, and moist curing at **20 °C / 95% RH** as generic metadata, not fresh-rheology test conditions. Mixing and rheometer protocols were unspecified.
